definitions.explanation: A counter for pairs of shoes, socks, and other footwear.

examples.japanese: {靴|くつ}を{一|いっ}{足|そく}{買|か}う。
examples.english: To buy one pair of shoes.
examples.notes: いっそく with small っ

examples.japanese: {靴|くつ}を{二|に}{足|そく}{買|か}いました。
examples.english: I bought two pairs of shoes.

examples.japanese: {靴下|くつした}は{何|なん}{足|ぞく}ありますか。
examples.english: How many pairs of socks do you have?
examples.notes: なんぞく with voiced ぞ

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{靴|くつ}を{三|さん}{足|ぞく}{買|か}いました。{黒|くろ}と{白|しろ}と{茶色|ちゃいろ}です。
examples.english: I bought three pairs of new shoes. Black, white, and brown.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}には{靴下|くつした}を{五|ご}{足|そく}{持|も}っていきます。{毎日|まいにち}{替|か}えるためです。
examples.english: I'll bring five pairs of socks on the trip. So I can change them every day.

notes:
{足|そく} is used for counting pairs of footwear including shoes, socks, slippers, etc. Common forms:
- {一|いっ}{足|そく} (one pair - with っ)
- {二|に}{足|そく}
- {三|さん}{足|ぞく} (voiced)
- {何|なん}{足|ぞく}. This counter emphasizes that footwear comes in pairs.
